Yahweh is using the question form for emphasis, to command Ezekiel to pronounce judgment on **the city of blood**. If your language can repeat words for intensification, it would be appropriate to do that here in your translation. If not, your language may have another way of expressing the intensification. Alternate translation: [will you surely judge]
Here, **blood** represents “murder.” If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [the city of murderers]

Yahweh is using the possessive form to describe a **city** that is characterized by **blood**, that is, by murder. If a speaker of your language would not use the possessive form for this, you could express this idea in another way. Alternate translation: [the city whose people commit murder]

Yahweh is using the question form to command Ezekiel to confront the city with its sins. If a speaker of your language would not use the question form for that purpose, you could translate this as a statement or as an exclamation. Alternate translation: [And make her know all her abominations!]

The pronoun **her** refers to the city, and here it means the people who live in the city. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [And you will make the people of the city know all their abominations]
If your language does not use a noun for the idea of **abominations**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [all the detestable things that she has done]
